source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Screen the client and all items for MR hazards and verify the MR status and conditions of implanted devices.","B":"Skip implant screening when the client reports having completed a previous MRI without difficulty.","C":"Leave small metallic objects in place when they are not attached to a large piece of equipment.","D":"Treat an implant with unknown MR status as safe unless symptoms or heating occur during the scan."}}
source_row.rationale: FDA guidance emphasizes screening people and objects for MRI hazards and verifying the MR safety status of implants before scanning. Option A is correct. Prior MRI exposure does not automatically establish present-device safety, small ferromagnetic objects can be hazardous, and an unknown implant should not be assumed safe.
source_row.source_detail: MRI safety screening: carefully screen people and objects entering the MR environment; implanted devices must be positively identified as MR Safe or MR Conditional under the specified conditions; unknown status should not be assumed safe. Current FDA MRI safety guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
